extracted.intended_audience: researchers and institutions preparing grant applications to the CDMRP Peer Reviewed Medical Research Program (PRMRP)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative expectations for researchers applying to the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Program's Peer Reviewed Medical Research Program (PRMRP); covers program vision/mission alignment, topic-area fit, review process, and other application requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Program Vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision – Improve the health, care, and well-being of all military Service Members, Veterans, and their families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should clearly demonstrate how the proposed research will improve health, care, or well‑being of Service Members, Veterans, or their families. Explicit linkage to the program's stated population and outcomes strengthens relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear scientific merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission – Encourage, identify, select and manage medical research projects of clear scientific merit that lead to impactful advances in health care of Service Members, Veterans and their Families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are expected to present sound, rigorous science. Reviewers will prioritize projects with well‑justified hypotheses, appropriate study design/methodology, and evidence that the work is scientifically credible and feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for impactful advances / translational potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Program is committed to supporting research that has the potential to profoundly impact the development and implementation of medical devices, drugs, and clinical guidance that will enhance the precision and efficacy of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate how results could lead to or accelerate development of devices, therapeutics, diagnostics, or clinical practice changes. Emphasis is placed on near‑term translational potential and measurable impact on prevention, diagnosis, or treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to military and near‑term readiness needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical research supported by the PRMRP to address near-term military needs including military and personal readiness, continues this tradition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should describe relevance to military operational or readiness priorities (e.g., force health, deployable solutions). Projects addressing near‑term needs for Service Members and their families are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit to program topic areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRMRP solicits proposals in specified topic areas (examples: autoimmune diseases and immunology, cardiovascular health, infectious diseases, neurological and psychological health, orthopedic and regenerative medicine, respiratory health and injury, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must fall within the PRMRP topic areas offered in the funding announcement for the fiscal year. Demonstrate explicit alignment to the selected topic area and the priorities described in program materials (program summary sheet, strategic plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforming Health Care through Innovative and Impactful Research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program emphasizes innovative approaches. Applications should highlight novel concepts, methods, or technologies and explain how they advance the field beyond existing approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of research duplication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to ensure proposed work does not duplicate existing funded research. Provide literature/funding context and justify the unique contribution of the proposal; describe how the project complements, not replicates, prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and administrative requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet the program's eligibility criteria (organizational, PI, and other administrative requirements) before submission. Follow the eligibility checklist in the program materials to confirm you are an eligible applicant and that required documents and certifications are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑tiered review expectations (scientific peer review + programmatic review)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will undergo peer review for scientific and technical merit and a programmatic review (programmatic panel) that considers program priorities, impact, and portfolio balance. Applicants should address both scientific rigor and programmatic relevance in submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer involvement / patient‑stakeholder perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer Involvement; Program Consumer Reviewer Requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PRMRP includes consumer reviewers in the evaluation process. Where relevant, applicants should describe potential benefits to patients/consumers and consider incorporating consumer‑relevant outcomes or input; anticipate that consumer reviewers will assess clarity of benefit to affected populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated management and program oversight compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Program oversight is provided by a programmatic panel with joint military service and interagency representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate appropriate management plans and an understanding of program oversight expectations, including potential liaison with military or interagency stakeholders when applicable.
